problem: Language-conditioned navigation policies (action tokens, diffusion/flow trajectory generators) use each scene-instruction annotation only to supervise one start-conditioned rollout, so they are near-goal but collide often, and modular VLM pipelines are brittle.
motivation: A scene plus target defines useful local guidance from many feasible locations, but trajectory supervision only reveals states visited by one rollout. BEV gives a metric common frame where a field can be queried and supervised anywhere, so dense workspace-level supervision could yield more precise and safer navigation with cheap inference.
key_idea: Predict a language-conditioned continuous 2D flow field over the BEV workspace (queried at arbitrary coordinates, supervised densely with procedurally generated potential-gradient fields) and obtain trajectories by Euler integration from any start.
insight: The supervision coverage ablation shows the gain comes from dense workspace supervision, not the field decoder: full-workspace CR 0.22, tube CR 0.61, on-trajectory CR 0.91 and FGE 0.34, worse than DP-T-DDPM (CR 0.78). Trajectory baselines reach the goal (FGE ~0.16) but collide in most episodes. The predicted magnitude matters for stable termination: unit-speed rollout raises CR to 0.57 and Curv to 1.68, and no stabilizer gives CR 1.00. Pseudo receding-horizon replanning does not help DP, so the gap is not due to open-loop execution.
method: Problem formulation: navigation as a goal-conditioned vector field v(x|I,l) on normalized BEV workspace [0,1]^2; trajectory obtained by integrating dτ/dt=v(τ|I,l) from start x0

Vision-language encoder: frozen SigLIP 2 B/16 vision and text towers, linear projection + LayerNorm, then L=4 transformer decoder layers (self-attn over BEV tokens, cross-attn to text tokens) producing context tokens C (d=768)

Query decoder: Gaussian Fourier positional encoding of coordinates as queries, 2 simplified decoder layers (cross-attention to C + FFN, no query self-attention), heads predict softplus magnitude and unit direction, V=M⊙D (15.36M head params)
Training: stratified jittered sampling of N_s=1000 query points on a g×g grid per instance, targets bilinearly sampled from annotated field; loss = cosine direction loss + λ·squared magnitude loss

Inference: query decoder on a dense grid (e.g. 100×100), forward Euler rollout of 100 steps with bilinear sampling and inverse-time rescaling v/((1-t)+β t^α) to get quasi-constant speed and soft-capped stop near goal

Procedural dataset: >500k BEV image-instruction samples from Matterport3D (245,604) and ScanNet (342,038), 1 top-down + 8 oblique views per region, template instructions with spatial modifiers; annotation via safety-cost-weighted Dijkstra geodesic distance plus obstacle inner repulsion, potential Φ, flow=-∇Φ scaled by distance-to-go, and backtracked reference trajectories

setting.backbone: Frozen SigLIP 2 Base (ViT-B/16) + 4-layer fusion transformer + 2-layer query decoder (trained)
setting.model_size: ~429.5M total parameters, of which 15.36M head; SigLIP2-B frozen
setting.training_data: Own procedurally annotated dataset, >500k BEV image-instruction-flow/trajectory samples from Matterport3D (90 scenes) and ScanNet (1,513 scenes), scene-wise train/val split; 50 epochs
setting.observation: Monocular RGB BEV image (top-down or high-oblique, calibrated) + text instruction + robot start position in image coordinates
setting.action_space: Continuous 2D flow field integrated into a trajectory (100-step Euler; 50 steps in real world) tracked by a differential-drive base
setting.simulator: Rendered offline from Matterport3D and ScanNet scenes (open-loop benchmark, no interactive simulator); real world with overhead camera
setting.privileged: Robot position from motion capture mapped to image coordinates via calibrated homography in the real world; overhead calibrated camera; GT semantic maps used only for training annotations

results: On strictly unseen scenes, CoFL cuts collision rate to 0.17-0.22 on Matterport3D (vs 0.68-0.91 for DP-family/VLM baselines, ~4x lower) with FGE 0.13-0.15 vs ~0.16-0.19 for the best DP variants, and is more accurate and safer on ScanNet (FGE 0.07-0.09, CR 0.35-0.40 vs CR 0.86+). It uses a 15M head vs 74-81M for DP, with ~15.8 ms latency. Zero-shot real-world: 85% on-target without obstacles and 100% with obstacles (CR 0.30).
limitations: Requires a calibrated BEV observation and externally provided robot position; real-world tests are in a controlled overhead-camera arena
Fixed clearance profile baked into the supervision, with no adjustable safety margin; collisions with reactive obstacles are frequent (CR 0.80) and small objects such as a box are weak

Benchmark is a self-built, open-loop, 2D dataset with synthetic template instructions and only a few evaluated regions, and baselines are limited (Gemini-Flash VLM, Diffusion Policy variants), with no comparison on standard VLN benchmarks
